description: Curated, non-sensitive agent output quality cases. Every case is a task the platform really routes, paired with structural success properties that can be checked offline — no keys, no wallets, no network.

cases.task: Compare permissive and copyleft open-source licences for a small team shipping a paid product, then recommend one. Answer in two sections: 'Findings' and 'Recommendation'.

successProperties.description: Answers both requested sections, so the recommendation can be found without reading everything.
Names concrete licences instead of speaking in the abstract.
Long enough to be substantive, short enough to stay a briefing.
A research briefing never narrates its own limitations.

humanReview: Is the recommendation actionable for a team that has never shipped a licence file before?
Would a lawyer call any statement a legal conclusion rather than a trade-off?

cases.task: Condense this release into a 'Highlights' list of exactly five bullets for non-technical stakeholders: added wallet reconnect retries; fixed a duplicated fee line in receipts; the run report is now exportable; trimmed the dashboard payload by 40%; removed the legacy demo key; the status endpoint now reports the queue depth.

successProperties.description: Stakeholders get a labelled list, not a wall of prose.
The task asked for exactly five bullets; more or fewer means the constraint was ignored.
A stakeholder bullet stays under thirty words.
Keeps internal vocabulary out of a stakeholder summary.

humanReview: Does each bullet describe an outcome a customer could notice?
Is anything materially important missing from the condensed list?

cases.task: From these monthly line items — object storage $840, managed database $1,260, egress $610, CI compute $180, log retention $95 — identify the two largest cost drivers and one concrete reduction for each.

successProperties.description: Names the two drivers the numbers actually point at.
Quantifies the drivers instead of describing them qualitatively.
Every reduction has a cost; the answer says which one it accepts.

humanReview: Is each proposed reduction plausible for a team of this size?
Does the analysis distinguish the two drivers from the next-largest item?

cases.task: Write a JavaScript function that retries an async call with exponential backoff and a maximum attempt count. Reply with a single fenced code block, then a two-line usage note.

successProperties.description: One runnable block — a diff of alternatives is not an answer.
The retry loop is bounded, not infinite.
Fits on a screen, so it can be read in review.

humanReview: Would this retry loop amplify an outage (no jitter, unbounded concurrency)?
Does the usage note describe the failure it surfaces, not just how to import it?
